sentences.text: Copper sulfate concentrations must be verified twice daily with a calibrated test kit before any additional dosing occurs. "Count the white spots for me," the vet said, "and tell me whether they've spread past the gill covers." Fin rot rarely reverses without pristine water; test ammonia daily, because medication breaks down and fouls a small volume fast. One level scoop of kanamycin per five gallons, added right after the fifty-percent water change — never guess the volume. Six days into the ich protocol and the spots are finally dropping off the tetras, though the water smells faintly of salt. Observation note, 21:40 — the discus took two bloodworms, first food accepted since transfer to the ten-gallon hospital setup. You raise the heat one degree every twelve hours, watching the thermometer, hoping the cories can handle the climb. After the formalin dip, the koi hung motionless near the surface for a terrifying minute, then righted herself and swam. Nobody warns you how loud a bare-bottom hospital setup gets when the airstone runs full blast at 3 a.m. The clown loach in QT bay three stopped eating yesterday, and this morning his caudal fin looks ragged at the edges. Those salt-grain specks scattered across the black molly? Classic ichthyophthirius, the parasite every hobbyist learns to dread. On the phone, the aquatic vet talked me through netting the gourami, her voice low and steady the whole time. Honestly I nearly cried when the little betta flared at his reflection again — first sign of life since we started the antibiotics. Each morning I siphon uneaten pellets off the bare glass bottom, checking the waste for stringy white feces that signal internal parasites. Three treatment rounds finished, and still she recommended a final salt dip before he could rejoin the community aquarium. He measures the praziquantel with a jeweler's scale, muttering that a milligram either way matters at this dosage. She logged the observation at 7 a.m.: gills pumping fast, angelfish hanging near the sponge filter, fins clamped tight. Frantic, I photographed the lesion under the desk lamp and texted it to the on-call aquatic veterinarian before midnight. Wasn't the whole point of the quarantine rack to catch this before it reached my display fish? Do I really have to keep him isolated for four full weeks if the fin rot has already cleared up? What is the meaning of the word tank?
